claims.statement: StoreBackend provides a persistent cross-thread filesystem facade over a caller-supplied or execution-context LangGraph BaseStore, validates namespace components to prevent wildcard lookup injection, and preserves text or base64 binary file content through Store values.

dcode non-interactive execution owns one headless stream session, gates shell execution through its resolved allow-list and explicit project-hook trust, resumes interrupt responses in a bounded turn loop, keeps agent response text on stdout in quiet mode, and returns exit code 124 when the turn budget is exceeded.

StoreConversationArchive keeps scoped, idempotent transcript records in a caller-owned metadata Store, permits optional indexing only through a separate vector Store, makes host-confirmed replies indexable, bounds retrieval scans, and records deletion progress so vector-first deletion can resume safely after interruption.

The release dependency-freshness workflow gates release-please PRs by resolving the release target, reporting minimum freshness, building one wheel, validating its dependency metadata against PyPI and sibling source Python constraints, and installing that wheel with dependencies resolved only from PyPI.

HooksRuntime freezes a client-owned hook configuration snapshot for a workspace, only permits project-hook execution when workspace trust was resolved, materializes thread and subagent transcripts outside graph state, and exposes the snapshot ID and configured server lifecycle events to the graph.

HookEngine runs matching command handlers concurrently with individual timeout and output limits but reduces them in stable configuration order; it uses a sanitized environment, reports handler progress best-effort, and turns invocation-projection failures into a fail-closed result only when a matching handler is configured to deny on error.

The hook fulfillment path rejects a request from another snapshot and deduplicates concurrent or repeated client execution by snapshot and invocation ID before returning a typed LangGraph resume value.

ServerHooksMiddleware checkpoints private hook state and a per-turn snapshot/event gate, rejects a resume whose hook context changes mid-turn, and emits server lifecycle requests only for configured events while keeping its bookkeeping out of public graph I/O and subagent result merges.

ServerHooksMiddleware evaluates pre-tool hooks before tool execution and approval routing, can deny calls or rewrite only eligible local execute commands, checkpoint-records completed calls for post-tool or post-failure handling before the next model call, and uses Stop decisions to optionally feed back into a bounded graph continuation.

create_cli_agent installs server-owned hook middleware on both main and subagent stacks, disables subagent Stop emission while retaining tool hooks, and places the main hook middleware after HITL so PreToolUse decisions resolve before approval routing.

ProgramStatusReporter produces validated, size-bounded OSC 7501 records, safely sanitizes and encodes display text, de-duplicates per-record reports, clears tracked subtrees and optionally cleans up at exit, and treats terminal writes as thread-safe best-effort output subject to the global terminal-escape opt-out.

AgentStatusTracker owns TUI status precedence and lifecycle: the newest blocker outranks working and prior outcome, starting work clears prior outcome, closing a blocker preserves errors but otherwise returns to idle, transcript-mounted blockers are removed on a new conversation, and close clears status permanently.

For dcode headless runs, cli_main publishes an initial working status and always publishes exit_status afterward; successful runs become done, known failures become error, and interrupts or unknown exit codes clear the terminal record so final status does not alter process exit behavior.

The release-please scope detector derives bump-worthy types and managed package exclusions from release-please configuration, reports multi-component fan-out for bump-worthy PR titles without itself failing the analysis, and treats excluded package paths such as tests and lockfiles as non-release-relevant.

The release-please scope workflow runs the detector and configuration from the trusted PR base revision, obtains changed files through the GitHub API and fails when that list is incomplete, then turns reported fan-out into the merge-facing check while allowing an explicit ci:allow-lockfile-release acknowledgement label.

create_deep_agent is the Deep Agents construction seam: it uses DeltaChannel-backed message state, protects filesystem and synchronous delegation middleware from profile exclusion, and builds a stack where caller middleware can replace named defaults before final profile-based tool exclusion.

dcode ModelConfig gives a present DEEPAGENTS_CODE_ environment variable precedence over its canonical counterpart, merges managed policy only on the default configuration path, and fail-closes a malformed declared models.allowed policy as deny-all; active allowlists support exact provider:model and provider:* entries.

CostAwareCodeInterpreterMiddleware makes JavaScript-dispatched subagent cost durable by assigning isolated child checkpoint namespaces, collecting idempotent receipt checkpoints after dispatched work settles, and returning the aggregate as a parent session-cost transfer without changing synchronous execution.

CodeInterpreterMiddleware gives each LangGraph thread a private QuickJS slot and can persist only thread-mode state as a bounded snapshot, optionally HMAC-authenticated before restore; it clears invalid snapshot state rather than executing it.

CodeInterpreterMiddleware exposes programmatic tool calling and optional subagent dispatch from an eval invocation, but its direct fs bridge and PTC calls bypass normal Deep Agents filesystem permission and per-tool HITL paths, so these options are capability boundaries rather than ordinary tool exposure.

DeepAgentRuntime compiles its initial Talon graph after resolving subagents and approvals, refreshes tools before each invocation, snapshots graph and approval state under a lock for the turn, and compiles replacement graphs before assigning them so failed reloads retain the existing runtime graph.

Unified evaluations validate and construct an expected per-model flat matrix before calling the reusable Harbor workflow, isolate best-effort LangSmith usage collection from the repository-writing result publisher, and pass the pre-expanded matrix with derived concurrency limits to Harbor.

The reusable Harbor workflow either expands a single dataset or accepts the unified flat matrix, caps its runner pool from the resulting matrix, validates credentials and untrusted run inputs before execution, and uses matching shard partitions plus empty-shard markers so aggregation can distinguish an intentional no-op from a missing result.
